correctness.rationale: For any two strings of equal parity, they coincide or are antipodal, so neither friendship nor opposition can change a bit at 0<alpha<1. Opposite parity implies exactly one agreeing and one disagreeing issue; generic strict thresholds guarantee exactly one of these two discussions flips the focal parity. Uniform issue sampling makes that probability 1/2, yielding symmetric birth-death probabilities i(N-i)/(2N^2). The finite chain absorbs a.s., bounded martingale stopping gives a/N and the second-difference equation yields the explicit harmonic sum. All update-level arithmetic was independently enumerated over 4,225 microstate/parameter combinations and the expectation recurrence for N=2..49. Equal-threshold boundary explicitly excluded.

originality.rationale: The claim is the simultaneous strong-lumpability of a nontrivial friend/enemy model and exact threshold-invariance of its terminal hitting-time law, not a new solution of the classical gambler ruin recurrence. The originating open main text treats terminal types, simulations and ODE symmetries, while exact classical voter laws apply only after the proved projection. Claim-history and mathematical-literature searches did not identify this model-specific projection. Residual priority uncertainty is recorded.

value.rationale: The motivating paper treats threshold dependence of convergence and long-lived pluralism for several issues; the result proves a substantive structural exception for exactly two issues. It determines the full finite-N time law and complementary-pair fixation probability uniformly for all heterogeneous issue weights and noncritical thresholds, rules out exponential two-issue metastability, and exhibits a real divergence between time-invariance and threshold-sensitive consensus/polarization type. This is a model-specific phase-invariance theorem, rather than an isolated numerical or normalization observation.
